questions.q: Which four people does the summary treat as Twitter's founders?
a: Jack Dorsey, Ev Williams, Biz Stone and Noah Glass
Ev Williams, Jack Dorsey, Dick Costolo and Biz Stone
Jack Dorsey, Biz Stone, Noah Glass and Dick Costolo
Ev Williams, Noah Glass, Dick Costolo and Jack Dorsey
questions.why: Lesson 1 names Williams, Dorsey, Stone and Glass as the four who shaped both the idea and its implementation.

questions.q: Why was Noah Glass pushed out of the company before Twitter launched?
a: He talked publicly about Twitter too early
He refused to fund the podcasting project
He sold his shares to a rival company
He leaked the company's financial records
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Noah was removed after blabbing about Twitter before it had even been launched.

questions.q: How does the summary reconcile its advice to never hire friends with its advice to always hire them?
a: Friendships caused conflict but made the idea possible
Friends should be hired only after a company succeeds
Friendship matters more in small firms than large ones
Hiring friends works only when roles are clearly split
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues Twitter needed all four friends to get off the ground, even though their closeness caused quarrels.

questions.q: What did the upside-down sign reading 'Let's make better mistakes tomorrow' stand for?
a: A commitment to steady improvement over perfection
A warning that careless errors would be punished
A joke about the company's messy finances
A rule that decisions must be reviewed daily
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the sign captured a promise to keep progressing rather than trying to eliminate every mistake.

questions.q: Who first proposed the status update idea and built an early prototype with Biz Stone?
a: Jack Dorsey
Noah Glass
Ev Williams
Dick Costolo
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Jack proposed the status update concept and, with Biz, built the first prototype.
